description: Gzip budget for the production bundle. Every budget is enforced by scripts/check-bundle-budgets.mjs after `npm run build`; raise a limit only with a matching reason, never to make a red build green.

budgets.name: Total JavaScript
budgets.reason: The app shell plus the lazily-shared charting stack. Scripts/check-bundle-budgets.mjs fails when the sum of gzip sizes grows past this.

budgets.name: Application chunk
budgets.reason: The entry chunk that every visitor downloads before charts render. Keep app code out of the vendor chunks. Raised from 65 KiB when the runtime observability stack (telemetry envelopes, health checks, error capture) and the feature-flag runtime landed together, and from 68 KiB when the telemetry egress boundary landed (per-envelope field allowlists, fail-closed endpoint policy, master-switch gating): measured, deliberate additions to the entry chunk, not drift. Raised from 71 KiB when Forecasting's single shared Promise.all split into per-widget queries (VAL-RES-004 through VAL-RES-007): the shared scoped-query and cursor-pagination primitives plus the per-widget loading, named-error, and focused-retry UI each widget renders instead of one page-level pass/fail. Raised from 73 KiB when scoped answers gained their metadata envelope (VAL-DATA-006, VAL-RES-008): the QueryResult type through the providers and hooks, the shared query-state components that render completeness warnings and as-of captions, the mount-time GTM_HEALTH publication, and the static-route failure surfaces. Raised from 75 KiB when the failure surfaces became truthful and race-safe: the retry-focus recovery region every recovered widget, manager book, Data Connections section, and book route shares (a successful retry lands focus on the named region instead of the document body), the stable operation-specific failure copy that replaces raw rejection prose, the Data Connections loading-versus-failure split, and the health refresh publication guard. Raised from 76 KiB when row pagination became an enforced seam contract (VAL-DATA-009): the shared pagination primitive with validated bounded page limits, opaque query- and epoch-bound cursors, and typed invalid/foreign/expired failures, plus the bounded multi-page window refresh that keeps a loaded window consistent after it outgrows one maximum-size page; measured at +735 bytes gzip against the prior commit. Raised from 77 KiB when Home and Partner Performance moved onto the scoped contract (VAL-DATA-014): sixteen scoped provider methods — performance summary, funnel, stage and type breakdowns, the bounded four-quarter revenue trend and eight-week activity series, goal progress, registration ops, leaderboard, manager and partner directories, certification profiles, and four cursor-paginated collections — implemented through the contract, the mock, and both wrapper providers, plus the two per-route query hooks the views now render from; measured at ~+2.8 KiB gzip against the prior commit. Raised from 80 KiB when Deal Reg Ops and Activity Tracking moved onto the scoped contract (VAL-DATA-015): one new cursor-paginated method (the Log Meetings classification week) through the contract, the mock, and both wrapper providers, the two per-route query hooks, and the per-card loading, named-error, focused-retry, and load-more surfaces the views render instead of the folded book; measured at ~+1.2 KiB gzip against the prior commit. Raised from 82 KiB for the scoped-route scope-identity and session-edit remediation: read-time scopeKey gating on every Home, Partner Performance, and Partner View aggregate so a phase, manager, partner, or slice change never renders the prior scope's figures under the new label; Partner Performance session prospects riding the activity and goal scopes; certification gating that starts only for a selected partner; and provider-scoped SessionEdits threaded into Partner View's revenue aggregates and pipeline windows; measured at ~+0.1 KiB gzip against the prior commit.

budgets.name: Recharts chunk
budgets.reason: Recharts and its redux/immer runtime. The heaviest direct dependency; a jump here is the earliest signal that a chart dependency was upgraded or pulled in eagerly.

budgets.name: Chart dependencies chunk
budgets.reason: victory-vendor and the d3 packages Recharts reaches through it.

budgets.name: Stylesheet
budgets.reason: Tailwind output. Keep utility growth and unused custom CSS from accumulating unnoticed.
